en.question: What inflation rate has the National Bank of Poland (NBP) targeted since 2004?

answers.text: Whatever the government sets each year

en.successMessage: Since 2004, NBP has targeted a 2.5% annual CPI change over the medium term, with a symmetric ±1 percentage point deviation band (edges: 1.5% and 3.5%). This is a target, not current inflation, a forecast or a guaranteed monthly outcome. CPI concerns a basket of prices, not the same change in every price. The band is not a loan or deposit interest rate.
en.retryMessage: Since 2004, NBP has targeted a 2.5% annual CPI change over the medium term, with a symmetric ±1 percentage point deviation band (edges: 1.5% and 3.5%). This is a target, not current inflation, a forecast or a guaranteed monthly outcome. CPI concerns a basket of prices, not the same change in every price. The band is not a loan or deposit interest rate.

A.pl: Zweryfikowany cel NBP jest dodatni i wynosi 2,5%, a nie 0%; nie jest nakazem utrzymania każdej ceny bez zmiany.
A.en: The verified NBP target is positive at 2.5%, not0%; it does not require every individual price to remain unchanged.

C.pl: 5% nie jest opisanym celem NBP; nie myl przykładowej wartości z oficjalnym celem.
C.en: 5% is not the stated NBP target; do not confuse an example value with the official target.

D.pl: Cel określa strategia polityki pieniężnej RPP/NBP, a nie dowolny coroczny wybór rządu.
D.en: The target is set in the MPC/NBP monetary policy strategy, not by an arbitrary annual government choice.

en.question: Why might a central bank choose a small positive inflation target?

answers.text: To make the currency worthless faster
It provides a margin against deflation risk and can aid price stability
Because higher prices are always good
To increase government tax revenue only

en.successMessage: A small positive target provides a margin against deflation risk and can help monetary policy operate. It does not guarantee economic growth or predictability of every price. The target concerns the rate of change in the general price level; positive inflation means that level is still rising. Specific targets differ across central banks.
en.retryMessage: A small positive target provides a margin against deflation risk and can help monetary policy operate. It does not guarantee economic growth or predictability of every price. The target concerns the rate of change in the general price level; positive inflation means that level is still rising. Specific targets differ across central banks.

A.pl: Celem jest stabilność cen, a nie przyspieszanie utraty wartości pieniądza.
A.en: The aim is price stability, not accelerating the loss of money’s value.

C.pl: Wyższe ceny nie są zawsze korzystne; znaczenie mają tempo zmian, dochody i sytuacja gospodarstwa.
C.en: Higher prices are not always beneficial; the pace of change, income and household circumstances matter.

D.pl: Wyłączny cel fiskalny nie wyjaśnia średniokresowego celu stabilności cen.
D.en: A purely fiscal aim does not explain a medium-term price stability objective.

assumptions: ECB reasoning is general monetary education; its2% euroarea target is not substituted for Poland’s NBP2.5% target.

en.question: What is a central bank's main tool for steering inflation?
en.successMessage: Policy interest rates are NBP’s main tool, but not its only one: open market operations and other instruments also play a role. They influence financing conditions, demand and inflation with lags and uncertain strength. NBP does not thereby set every price or the interest rate of every contract; banks’ offers can differ.

en.question: When a central bank raises interest rates, what typically happens?

answers.text: Borrowing gets cheaper and spending jumps
Borrowing can become more expensive, weakening demand and inflation pressure

en.successMessage: Higher rates can raise the cost of new or variable-rate borrowing, weakening demand and inflation pressure; effects are delayed and uncertain. Repricing terms and timing depend on the contract; an agreed fixed-rate period need not reprice immediately. Slower positive inflation means prices rise more slowly, not that they fall. This is not a payment forecast or a borrowing decision.
en.retryMessage: Higher rates can raise the cost of new or variable-rate borrowing, weakening demand and inflation pressure; effects are delayed and uncertain. Repricing terms and timing depend on the contract; an agreed fixed-rate period need not reprice immediately. Slower positive inflation means prices rise more slowly, not that they fall. This is not a payment forecast or a borrowing decision.

A.pl: To odwrotność opisanego typowego kanału: podwyżka stóp może ograniczać, a nie pobudzać popyt kredytem.
A.en: This reverses the typical channel described: higher rates can restrain rather than stimulate borrowing-led demand.

C.pl: Warunki kredytu i oszczędzania mogą się zmieniać, choć nie jednakowo i nie od razu dla wszystkich.
C.en: Borrowing and saving conditions can change, though not equally or immediately for everyone.

D.pl: Nie ma zasady, że rachunki oszczędnościowe zawsze mają oprocentowanie 0%.
D.en: There is no rule that savings accounts always pay0% interest.

en.question: What does GDP (Gross Domestic Product) measure?

answers.text: The total savings of all citizens
The value of final goods and services produced in an economy over a period
The amount of cash in circulation

en.successMessage: GDP describes the value of final production in an economy over a period. In GUS’s production approach, gross value added plus taxes on products less subsidies are counted; intermediate goods are not added again to final output. GDP is not total savings, personal income or a complete measure of wellbeing or income distribution.
en.retryMessage: GDP describes the value of final production in an economy over a period. In GUS’s production approach, gross value added plus taxes on products less subsidies are counted; intermediate goods are not added again to final output. GDP is not total savings, personal income or a complete measure of wellbeing or income distribution.

A.pl: Oszczędności to zasób środków, a PKB opisuje produkcję za okres, nie sumę sald obywateli.
A.en: Savings are a stock of funds; GDP describes production over a period, not the sum of citizens’ balances.

C.pl: Gotówka w obiegu jest zasobem pieniądza, a nie wartością produkcji finalnej za okres.
C.en: Cash in circulation is a stock of money, not the value of final production over a period.

D.pl: Dług publiczny to stan zobowiązań, a nie produkcja finalna w danym okresie.
D.en: National debt is a stock of liabilities, not final production during a period.

assumptions: Simplified final-use definition alongside GUS value-added approach, no GDP level/growth statistic or personal score.

en.question: Why can a persistent fall in the general price level (deflation) be harmful?

answers.text: It makes everyone richer with no downside
It can delay some purchases, weaken demand and raise the real debt burden
It has no effect on the economy

en.successMessage: A persistent fall in the general price level can delay some purchases, weaken demand and increase the real burden of unchanged nominal debt. These are possible mechanisms, not an inevitable spiral in every situation. A single discount or slower positive inflation does not mean deflation. This is not a reason to postpone urgent essential needs or required repayments.
en.retryMessage: A persistent fall in the general price level can delay some purchases, weaken demand and increase the real burden of unchanged nominal debt. These are possible mechanisms, not an inevitable spiral in every situation. A single discount or slower positive inflation does not mean deflation. This is not a reason to postpone urgent essential needs or required repayments.

A.pl: Spadek cen nie oznacza korzyści bez kosztów dla każdego; dochody, zatrudnienie i zadłużenie także mają znaczenie.
A.en: Falling prices do not mean cost-free benefits for everyone; income, employment and debt also matter.

C.pl: Deflacja nie gwarantuje wzrostu płac; przebieg wynagrodzeń zależy od innych warunków.
C.en: Deflation does not guarantee higher wages; wage developments depend on other conditions.

D.pl: Trwałe spadki ogólnego poziomu cen mogą wpływać na popyt i realny ciężar długu.
D.en: Persistent declines in the general price level can affect demand and the real debt burden.

assumptions: Real-debt statement holds nominal debt unchanged; no individual repayment calculation or claim every price/wage falls.
